neighbours.label: good intentions or meaning well, especially when it fails (they mean well, well intentioned, well-meaning, good intentions, motives are good), as opposed to 'well' and 'intentions' with other meanings
fire: Her neighbors mean well but they never stop talking.
The policy was well intentioned but badly carried out.
Well-meaning relatives gave him far too much advice.
Sometimes good intentions can make matters worse.
While the mayor's motives are good, the plan will fail.
However well meaning, the charity did more harm than good.
The new rules, though well-intentioned, confused the staff.
I know you mean well, but please stop calling.
quiet: Her neighbors sing well but they never stop talking.
The policy was well known and quickly carried out.
Wealthy relatives gave him far too much money.
Sometimes heavy storms can make the roads worse.
While the mayor's car is good, the plan is to walk.
His stated intentions were to buy the land and build.
The new rules, though well-printed, are on the wall.
I know you sleep well, so please stop calling.

notes: 'His true intentions were to steal' reached 0.26 in a probe, so the word alone carries some activation. One near miss above is similar.
